refuted_claims:
1. "Run 2 keys 22/25 correct at page scope (F1 14/14, F2 8/11) ... all 3 defects are caught by a free mechanical page-scope re-derivation". The explorer's own v2/out/scope/scope_report.json marks key_holds=false for FOUR F2 items: #15, #18, #21 and #24. For #24 the page-scope winner is Indira Gandhi International Airport, against the key Chhatrapati Shivaji. The report instead files #24 under "text defects (key unaffected): omits the year". Under one consistent standard, page-scope accuracy is 21/25 (F2 7/11; exact 95% CI 0.64-0.96). Otherwise the free check raises a false alarm on multi-year pages. Either way "caught all 3" is circular, because the same check was used to define the defects, so it is not a validated detector. The SearchQA fixes were never re-run.

2. "Exact or N items solved 17/24 (0.71) against real meta-absent cells 71/128 (0.55)", read as "generated items are easier". All 30 valid run-1 items contain the meta option: 16 have it present but not as the key (the M- counterfactual), and 14 have it as the key. So 16 of the 24 pooled items are not meta-absent. The only truly meta-absent generated items are run-2 N: 5/8 (CI 0.24-0.91) against 0.555 real, which is no evidence of a difference. Also, every pilot solve used "contract first, no Skill" (pilot/common.py solve), while the real stage-entry cells carried the I-ds or E-ds parent Skill. Difficulty comparisons are therefore not like-for-like, although the M+ gap (5/21 vs 1/100) is large enough to survive this.

3. "Non-inferiority with a 3-point margin at n=200: harmless 0.94-0.95, 5-point harm 0.17, 8-point harm 0.007", and "a 3-point harm ... is a coin flip at every n, as it should be". c4_power.py passes a rule when the observed delta is at least -3 points. That is a point-estimate threshold, not a non-inferiority test: a proper NI test passes a margin-sized harm at most 5% of the time, not 53%. My simulation, with the same noise model, used a one-sided 95% NI test. At n=200 x 2 runs it passes a harmless rule only 0.45 of the time (D6's calibration) or 0.56 (corrected calibration). For 90% harmless pass at a 3-point margin you need about 550 items x 2 runs or about 300 x 4 runs; a 4-point margin needs about 300 x 2 runs. 200 x 2 runs supports only a 5-point margin (harmless 0.91, 5-point harm 0.05). So "about 200 items per similar target per step" holds only for the lenient threshold or a 5-point margin.

4. Noise calibration. c4_power.py treats 30/194 as disagreement between two single runs, 2p(1-p). The measured 30/194 is the number of items whose 2-run mean changed between screen and confirm for the same text. The unstable share is therefore 0.276, not 0.378. The error is conservative and does not rescue point 3. The "v3 C4' is a coin flip" conclusion survives both calibrations: on 8-12 items a harmless rule passes 0.60-0.68 and an 8-point harm passes 0.22-0.36.

5. Cost: "about 1.5M tokens per target-step for LiveMath- or SearchQA-style, about 4.5M OfficeQA-style" (verdict_cn: 150万-450万 per step). The per-cell costs used (811 and 1,075) come from Skill-less solves. Measured v3 stage-entry training cells under the task-card parent (I-ds) cost 3,969 tokens (LiveMath), 4,088 (SearchQA), 7,927 (OfficeQA) and 4,273 (SpreadsheetBench). Under the empty scaffold they cost 1,251, 1,236, 4,690 and 2,010. The Skill adds about 2.3-3.2k tokens to every cell. At D6's own 1,200 cells per target-step, the primary chain costs about 4.7-5.1M (LiveMath/SearchQA-style) and about 10M (OfficeQA-style), i.e. 2-3x the estimate. A 3-point NI margin multiplies this by about 2.75 again. The OfficeQA stage has two forward targets once SpreadsheetBench is added. The validity-study estimate (4-6M per target) also omits the Skill overhead and the real-pool cells.

6. "A 2-of-3 tiebreak would raise run 2's yield from 22/36 to 30/36 with 0 wrong values" (design: "accepts a value only if two agree and one of them is a program"). In tiebreak_probe.py the pair (GLM code, GLM stated value) can outvote the independent deepseek program. That configuration occurred in 0 of the 16 probe cases: run-1 code bugs had no stated value, and every run-2 mismatch had code different from belief. So the risky case is untested. As specified, the L2 rule "must agree exactly" is void whenever GLM's code matches its own belief, for example an index-shift bug like run-1 #34 that GLM also believes. The independent program must be one of the agreeing pair.

7. Validity study: "the empty scaffold against the task-card seeds is a known large positive effect; placebos are known nulls". That effect was measured on SearchQA (cal-1 is SearchQA only). On the forward targets' real training cells (v3 stage entry, same items, 2 runs), I-ds minus E-ds is +4.7 points on OfficeQA (paired SE 3.2, CI -1.6 to +11.0, 74 items) and -4.5 points on LiveMath (SE 2.9, CI -10.1 to +1.1, 100 items). With about 6 variants, mostly nulls whose delta sign is noise, sign agreement cannot validate a panel at rule-sized effects (1-5 points).

8. Registration conflicts presented as engineering details. Registration v6 §2.2: for a benchmark not yet reached, the learning history uses none of its real items or labels, only its public task card and researched public material. §8: the generator sees no items of these benchmarks. §2: test sets are read only at evaluation. The LiveMath public card (manifest "cards") never mentions the meta option. D6's mirror panel (meta sentence verbatim; M+:N = 68:87 with meta always the key) is derived from LiveMath training labels. The validity study uses the forward targets' real training pools, OfficeQA option (a) uses the real OfficeQA corpus, and the test-hash exclusion reads test-panel identifiers outside evaluation. Each needs an owner re-registration or a label-free design.

Minor: verdict_cn says the v3 pathway "常把答案写进题干" (often writes the answer into the question), but only 2 of the 10 kept items do.
confirmed_claims:
Each item below was checked against the data on the new machine, using training files only. The manifest pins both dev_panel.json files as train.

Target facts (all reproduced exactly):
- LiveMath pool: 155 tasks; key letters A25 B34 C34 D22 E40; meta option in 68/155 items and the key in 68/68; meta positions A12 B10 C17 D11 E18; "strongest" in 114/155 questions; 14/775 options of 40 characters or fewer; question length median 598 (137-1,992).
- Stage-entry pass counts: SearchQA 310/400 and 297/400; OfficeQA 37/148 and 30/148; LiveMath 66/200 and 75/200.
- LiveMath split: meta-key cells pass 1/100 (I-ds 0/50, E-ds 1/50); meta-absent cells pass 71/128. Only 57 of the 100 LiveMath stage items are in dev_panel.json; the rest come from the val partition merged into the training pool (registration §2).
- Failure codes: SearchQA (n=193) D1 37%, D2 25%, D3 7% (69% answer-form), D4 13%, D5 10%; OfficeQA (n=229) 27/38/17/6/9%; LiveMath (n=259) D1 63%, D2 0.
- 6 of the 10 SearchQA-stage proposals target codes D1-D3.
- OfficeQA: 39/50 numeric answers; maximum context 29,325 characters; keyword union 20/50 (6/6/4/3/3/2).
- ALFWorld train split: 2,435 task folders, 3,553 games, 7 type prefixes.

LiveMath-style correctness (my own brute force and closed forms, separate from the explorer's audit):
- Run 2: 22/22 values, and 22/22 keys after re-deriving every option tag.
- Dropped specs: the code was right in #2, #6, #18, #28, #30 and #35; it was wrong in #31 (91; the true value is 87).
- Run 1: every value matches except the known #34 bug (true F30 = 832,040). The meta key is still correct there because only "divisible by 8" is true.
- So keys 52/52 holds.

Solver results:
- Run 2 by form: M+ 3/7 (all 4 failures picked the weaker true claim), M- 6/7, N 5/8; key letters D 9/22.
- 16/16 meta-key failures picked a claim that is true under the real value.
- In #3, #9 and #12 the solver computed the exact value, then chose the weaker claim.
- On real meta-key items the solver picks the meta option 1/100 times, and 28/100 replies explicitly dismiss it ("not a concrete statement", "a distractor"). This partly supports reading D1 as a meta-option reading failure.

Tiebreak probe: 31/31 agreement on correct values and 4/4 true values against code bugs, matching probe.json.

v3 forward smoke test:
- The frozen snapshot was first on the import path.
- Both panels came out short (7 and 3 items).
- LiveMath material returned "no_material" in 3 of 5 rounds through valid role calls, so this is a design outcome, not a network failure.
- 2 of 7 OfficeQA-style items state the answer, and 4 of 7 are bare single-cell lookups.
- All 3 LiveMath-style items are keyed "A", with literal formulas.

Power: v3 C4' on 8-12 items is a coin flip under both noise calibrations.

Statistics and totals: every quoted Clopper-Pearson interval is correct; the zero-defect bound is correct (n=60 gives 4.87%); the pilot total of 482,281 tokens adds up.

Literature: Reasoning Gym (NeurIPS 2025, more than 100 generators and verifiers) and SpreadsheetBench's judge-style scoring with several test spreadsheets per instruction are confirmed.

Hard rules: D6 did not write into the v3 run directory (its ledger was last modified 10/20 10:18).
missing:
Prior art not cited:
- DyVal (Zhu et al., ICLR 2024): generated reasoning items with controllable difficulty.
- GSM-Symbolic (Mirzadeh et al., ICLR 2025): templated variants shift accuracy and raise variance, which bears on fidelity and on the unmeasured instability.
- AutoIF (Dong et al., ICLR 2025): verification code cross-checked by unit tests, close to L2.
- Benchmark Agreement Testing (Perlitz et al., NeurIPS 2025): validating one benchmark against another is unreliable with few models.

Not piloted:
- No re-run after the SearchQA fixes.
- The F3 answer-form family, which covers 69% of real SearchQA failures.
- The OfficeQA- and SpreadsheetBench-style generators, the two forward targets that matter most.
- Difficulty targeting (parent passes 50-80%) is shown for no style: SearchQA-style 91% with context, OfficeQA-style 14/14, LiveMath M+ 24%. The 50-80% target also contradicts mirroring LiveMath's real ~35%.

Audit layer:
- The L3/L3' auditor is neither specified nor costed. In this pilot, the "independent audit" was done by the same agent that wrote the generators.
- Workload: 60 items per family x about 15-20 families, plus 5 per family per step.
- Generated-item instability is unmeasured (each item was solved once).

A validity design that could work:
- Constructed Skill variants with large known harms and gains (for example, forced verbose answers on SearchQA-style items).
- At least 10 variants, compared by rank correlation.
- More runs on the real pool.

Rule echo in v3 panels: material chosen "on the topic of the rule" makes the panel echo the rule. In the smoke test, a "verify the candidate" rule got "Verify this by computing ..." items, and a precision rule got items that say "carry all intermediate values at full precision". Such panels test the rule on its own topic, so they are biased toward passing. D6's rule-independent mirror panels fix this; the report should say so.

Data gaps:
- 43 of the 100 LiveMath stage items (val partition) were not inspected; the 68/68 fact rests on the 155 dev items.
- ALFWorld: 365 of the 2,435 train folders are pick_and_place_with_movable_recep, outside the 6 standard types. The registered test size of 134 equals ALFWorld's valid_unseen split, so train games are probably disjoint by construction (claim; the test panel was not opened).

notes_cn: 复核结论：部分成立。属实：仿LiveMath（数学选择题测试集）的52道生成题，我用自己的程序逐题重算，答案全对；训练数据统计和上一版（v3）通过数也核对无误。需更正：一、仿SearchQA（检索问答）题按其自己的全页复查，答对21道而非22道；二、每步200道题只够“最多容许掉5分”的严格检验，只容许掉3分需约550道；三、成本漏算了每次作答都附带的技能文本，主链每步每个相似测试集约500万到1000万token（模型计算量单位），是原估计的2到3倍；四、按LiveMath真题的答案规律出题，违反“还没学到的测试集不得用其真题和答案”的登记规定，需负责人决定。生成题能否代表真题仍未验证。
